description: Curated parameter facts for Neural DSP Morgan Amps Suite. Hand-maintained: this is the contract the generator writes against. It contains no Neural DSP code, audio, or preset content - only parameter names, units, and ranges needed to read and write presets for a licensed copy of the plugin.

/version.note: Plugin format version. Never write this - it is the file's own schema tag.

/selectedAmp.note: Chooses the live amp. All three amp modules exist in every preset, so any template can reach any amp. User-verified in the plugin.

pr12Amp/pr12Volume.note: PR12 is a 12W Princeton-style amp; past roughly 60% it starts to break up.

pr12Amp/pr12Dwell.note: Spring-reverb decay. Morgan added it to the original Princeton circuit specifically so you can run a high reverb mix without washing the tone out — so for a wet-but-defined clean, raise pr12Reverb and keep dwell moderate.

sw50rAmp/sw50rLevel.note: Master volume - does not add gain.

sw50rAmp/sw50rTrebleBoost.note: THE STORED KEY NAME IS MISLEADING. Writing this key moves the control the plugin itself publishes as `SW50R Bass Emphasis`, so ON thickens the low end — it is not a treble boost. The config reference's `bassEmphasis` was right and this manifest was wrong; the key name is the one thing here that is not evidence. SW50R's actual brightness switch is the separate `sw50rBright`, drawn on the amp panel as a sun/moon toggle right next to this one. This control is drawn as a treble-clef/bass-clef toggle, so OFF is not neutral — it is the treble position. Measured against the plugin — see docs/measuring-against-the-plugin.md.

sw50rAmp/sw50rInputMode.note: Two input jacks, not a bright/normal toggle: `false` selects the control's `High` position and `true` selects `Low`. High is the default and the hotter input; Low is the padded one, which is the config reference's `-6_DB`. Measured against the plugin — see docs/measuring-against-the-plugin.md.

ac20Amp/ac20Cut.note: Treble cut, borrowed from the Vox power-amp Cut control: HIGHER = DARKER. It works backwards from a normal tone knob. An earlier note in this repo claimed the opposite; the config reference, the control's name, and Morgan's own description of it as attenuating highs all agree on higher = darker. Check by ear in five seconds: raise it and listen for the top end to go.

ac20Amp/ac20BassTreble.note: A two-position voicing switch the plugin publishes as `AC20 Bass Cut`: `false` selects the `Bass` position, `true` selects `Treble`. So ON is the brighter, tighter voicing and OFF is the fuller one — the config reference's `bassCut` reading was the right one. Measured against the plugin — see docs/measuring-against-the-plugin.md.

ac20Amp/ac20Power.note: Not a selector: a continuous power control, stored 0.0–1.0 and shown as 0–100%. The example preset's `1` is 100%, not selector index 1.

compressor/compressorRelease.note: Fast/slow release toggle: `true` is Fast, `false` is Slow. Measured against the plugin — see docs/measuring-against-the-plugin.md.

tremolo/tremoloRate.note: Used when tremoloSync is off. The config reference said 0.05–5.0 Hz; the plugin's real range is 0.15–15 Hz, so fast tremolo above 5 Hz is available and was previously rejected.

tremolo/tremoloSync.note: When on, tremoloSyncNote sets the rate and tremoloRate is ignored.

tremolo/tremoloSyncNote.note: Prefer `tremoloRate` in Hz with `tremoloSync` off. Note that this table is NOT the same as the delay's: tremolo starts at 1/32T, so every index is shifted by two against `enums.delayNote`. Used only when `tremoloSync` is on.

cabParameters/leftMicType.note: Index 10 is `Custom IR`, which is not a mic at all: it tells the cab to use `leftChosenIRFilePath` instead. Only set it together with a valid path — selected with no file, the plugin shows `Custom IR / No File`. Conversely, clearing the path without moving this selector off 10 leaves the preset in that same broken state, which is why --strip-irs resets both. Verified in the plugin UI and against the Audio Unit.

cabParameters/leftCabPan.note: Not a selector: a signed pan position. Negative is left, positive is right, 0 is centre; the plugin displays -25 as `25 L` and +25 as `25 R`. The ends are hard limits, so this cab cannot be panned past 50.

cabParameters/leftRoomMicType.note: NO CONTROL FOR THIS EXISTS IN THE PLUGIN UI. The cab page has two mics and a Room Send level; there is nowhere to choose a room mic type. The Audio Unit exposes it as a reserved slot named `R3`/`R6` with no value names, unlike every other parameter, which is the same story from the other side. It accepts 0, 1 and 2 and rewrites anything higher to 0. Leave it at whatever the template holds: a value written here cannot be seen, checked, or explained to the user. Verified in the UI and against the Audio Unit — see docs/measuring-against-the-plugin.md.

cabParameters/leftChosenIRFilePath.note: Absolute path to a third-party IR on the machine that saved the preset. Empty means 'use the internal mic', stored byte-identically to how an IR-free preset holds it. Clearing it is reversible, but it does change the sound. Use --strip-irs to make a preset portable.

delay/delayTime.note: Used when delaySync selects free-running mode.

delay/delaySync.note: You usually do not need it: leave it at whatever the template has and set `delayTime` in ms. `DAW` follows the host tempo and makes `delaySyncNote` the thing that sets the time; `Free` uses `delayTime`; `Tap` waits for the user to tap.

delay/delaySyncNote.note: PREFER `delayTime` IN MILLISECONDS INSTEAD: packs/timing.py converts a tempo and a division into exact ms (120 BPM + '1/8 dotted' = 375 ms), which needs no selector and leaves the delay free-running. Only use this selector when the user wants the delay to follow host tempo changes, which also needs `delaySync` on `DAW`.
